Documentation / Developer / Layout Properties panel

Layout Properties panel

The docked panel consumes a value snapshot and a commit callback. A row carries an operation ID and a typed control value. It has no project configuration or Layout dependencies. A future workspace provider can supply its own IDs, snapshot, and command adapter.

The Layout provider uses the active page name and ordered LayoutElementRef identities. Selection changes and Layout document commits queue one refresh. The Layout manager revision and current ordered context are checked before accepting a control event. Replacing the project, changing pages, removing an element, or updating document history therefore invalidates stale edits even before the queued repaint. The GL render and mouse-motion paths never query the panel.

Document edits call the existing Layout manager operations. Element geometry uses SetElementFrame in the neutral document edit service. The operation validates before publishing one snapshot, retains unedited viewport residuals, and quantizes integer frames by the existing rules. An unchanged displayed millimeter value is a no-op. Position-only preview updates reuse existing Layout rasters. Resizing or editing an element marks its individual raster dirty.

The text inspector reads the same formatted runs used by Layout rendering and PDF. Inline style changes apply one property to the whole text box. They use the existing wx rich-text buffer, font catalog control, installed-font property, and legacy color rules. Mixed formatting, unsupported rich text, and recovery archives are inspected read-only and use the existing Edit Text transaction. The text content itself opens in the full editor.

wxAUI owns panel docking. The stable LayoutProperties pane is hidden outside Layout Mode. Legacy perspectives retain their existing panes and receive the new pane on the right. A separate user-only Layout perspective and explicit visibility preference preserve docking and hiding without a project mutation.

Native verification

LayoutExportInput exercises the native controls and the shared rich-text adapter on all CI platforms. On Linux, run the workspace smoke with the application's objects and the platform's wxAUI implementation.

cmake --build build/wsl-x64-debug --target Perastage
xvfb-run -a -s '-screen 0 1600x1000x24' \
  env LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE=1 python3 tests/run_viewport_regression_smoke.py \
  build/wsl-x64-debug --source tests/layout_properties_workspace_smoke.cpp

In a Debug build on Windows, macOS, or Linux, open Layout Mode and verify the left page list, central canvas, and right pane at normal and high display scales. Resize and float Properties, switch to 2D, 3D, and Inspector, and return. Hide Properties, repeat the switches, reopen it through View, and then restart to verify persistence. Opening a legacy perspective should keep its other positions. Select a fixed-scale viewport and press Enter on an unchanged frame value, then edit a single dimension and check Undo/Redo. Select several elements, inspect mixed values, and apply a command from the Alignment toolbar.

Select a legacy Text Box with mixed colors and a recovery archive. Verify the inspector leaves its XML intact, the Layout and PDF render inherited ink in black, and Edit Text still preserves the original archive. For a uniform box, change the color to white, apply a font and alignment, and compare Layout preview, PDF, PSTG reopen, and a portable Layout template round trip.
